description: Generate Git commit messages with one click or ⌥↩ (Alt+Enter) in the commit box. Uses the Claude Code CLI or LLMs available in VS Code.
untrustedWorkspaces.description: IntelliCommit needs the built-in Git extension, which is disabled in Restricted Mode. Workspace-level prompt and diff settings are ignored until the workspace is trusted.
command.generate.title: Generate commit message
command.stop.title: Stop generating commit message
command.selectSource.title: Select LLM Source
config.model: VS Code LLM used when the source includes VS Code LLMs, by model `id`. Leave empty (the default) to pick automatically from `#intellicommit.preferredModels#`, which favors cheap, fast models. The available models depend on your installed extensions, so they can't be listed here: IntelliCommit writes their ids to its log (**Output › IntelliCommit**) each time it checks them.
config.preferredModels:
Ordered list of name fragments used to pick a VS Code LLM when `#intellicommit.model#` is empty. Each fragment is matched case-insensitively against the model's id, family and name; the first fragment that matches any available model wins. If nothing matches, the cheapest available model (judged by its name) is used.

Tip: avoid very short fragments such as `mini`, which can match the middle of unrelated model names.
config.style: Commit message style. All styles follow traditional Git conventions: imperative subject, ideally at most 50 characters (72 maximum), no trailing period, blank line, body wrapped at 72 columns.
config.style.traditional: Capitalized, imperative subject line, e.g. "Fix null check in config loader".
config.style.conventional: Conventional Commits 1.0: "type(scope): subject", e.g. "fix(config): handle missing file".
config.style.gitmoji: One leading gitmoji followed by a traditional subject, e.g. "🐛 Fix null check in config loader".
config.style.auto: Follow the style used by most of the last 10 commits; without a clear pattern, use conventional.
config.language: Language of the generated message, e.g. `English` or `German`. `auto` uses English unless the recent commits are clearly written in another language.
config.customInstructions: Extra instructions appended to the prompt, e.g. "Mention the ticket number from the branch name." At most 2000 characters.
config.excludeGlobs: Glob patterns for files whose diff is not sent to the model (lockfiles, minified or generated files). Excluded files are still listed by name. Patterns without a `/` match the file name in any folder.
config.maxDiffChars: Hard cap on the number of diff characters sent to the model (1,000 to 100,000). The diff is also limited by the selected model's input token limit, whichever is smaller. Larger values describe big changes in more detail but use more tokens.
config.onExistingText: What to do when the commit message box already contains text.
config.onExistingText.replace: Replace the existing text. It is restored if generation is cancelled or fails.
config.onExistingText.append: Append the generated message below the existing text.
config.onExistingText.ask: Ask each time whether to replace or append.
config.source: Where IntelliCommit gets its LLM from. With a fallback option, the second source is used only when the first one is unavailable (for example, the Claude Code CLI is not installed, or no VS Code LLMs exist). Each source has its own model setting in the sections below. You can also change it with [Select LLM Source](command:intellicommit.selectSource) or from the **…** menu at the top of the Source Control view.
config.source.claudeCodeThenVsCode.label: Claude Code CLI, fallback to VS Code LLMs
config.source.vsCodeThenClaudeCode.label: VS Code LLMs, fallback to Claude Code CLI
config.source.claudeCode.label: Claude Code CLI only
config.source.vsCode.label: VS Code LLMs only
config.source.claudeCodeThenVsCode: Use the Claude Code CLI with your Claude sign-in; use VS Code LLMs if it is unavailable.
config.source.vsCodeThenClaudeCode: Use LLMs provided by VS Code extensions; use the Claude Code CLI if none are available.
config.source.claudeCode: Use only the Claude Code CLI.
config.source.vsCode: Use only LLMs provided by VS Code extensions.
config.claudeCode.model: Claude model used when the source includes the Claude Code CLI. Listed from cheapest to most expensive; each option uses the latest model of that family. Haiku (the default) is fast and uses the least of your plan.
config.claudeCode.model.haiku: Fastest; uses the least of your plan. Recommended for commit messages.
config.claudeCode.model.opus: Very capable; slower and uses more of your plan.
config.claudeCode.path: Full path to the `claude` executable. Leave empty to find it on your `PATH` and in the default install locations.
config.claudeCode.model.fable: Most capable; slowest and uses the most of your plan. Usually more than commit messages need.
